correctness.rationale: The explicit translation makes the two graph heights and gradients agree at an interior base point. The graph-difference Hessian is exactly diagonal with one positive and one negative eigenvalue, so the Morse lemma gives a local product normal form. Its sublevel set has area comparable to \(\delta\log(1/\delta)\), and vertical overlap contributes another factor \(\delta\). The matching upper bound is Theorem 1.5(b) with the fixed parameter gap \(19/81\). Cinematic nondegeneracy and the hyperbolic sign condition were checked directly on the full displayed parameter rectangle.

value.rationale: The extra logarithm is exactly the quantitative distinction between the elliptic and hyperbolic parts of the fresh three-dimensional anti-compression theorem. The example proves that this loss cannot be removed uniformly and identifies a geometric saddle mechanism inside one of the source’s canonical power families. This closes a natural sharpness question for the new theorem while explicitly separating that conclusion from the still different maximal-operator problem.
